title: Selections from the Writings of the Bab
author: The Bab
description: A compilation of the writings of the Bab (Siyyid Ali-Muhammad Shirazi, 1819-1850), the Persian prophet whose 1844 declaration began the Babi movement and who is regarded by Baha'is as the herald and forerunner of Baha'u'llah. Prepared by the Research Department of the Universal House of Justice and translated by Habib Taherzadeh (1976), it presents extracts from his major works, including the Qayyumu'l-Asma (commentary on the Surah of Joseph), the Persian Bayan, the Seven Proofs, the Book of Names and his addresses and prayers. Themes include the cyclical renewal of divine revelation, the expected advent of 'Him Whom God shall make manifest', the spiritual meaning of resurrection, judgement and paradise, the unity of the Prophets, and intense devotional praise of God. The Bab's ornate, symbol-laden style draws on Shi'i esoteric and Shaykhi thought, making this volume valuable both as Baha'i scripture and as a primary source for nineteenth-century Persian messianism and Islamic mysticism.
